data.narrative:
Ayar Labs, a Series E chip and semiconductor company founded by Mark Wade and Vladimir Stojanovic, carries a current post-money valuation of $3.75B following $870M+ in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a comp universe of 8 private peers in the semiconductor frontier-tech space, including Etched ($5.0B, Series E), Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), and SambaNova Systems ($11.0B, Series A), alongside 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

Two triangulation methods apply to this valuation. The Stage-Progression method, applying a typical 1.4x Series E step-up multiplier to the $3.75B last post-money, implies $5.2B. The Peer-Median method across 8 same-sector comparables yields $2.3B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $11.0B. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of disclosed revenue figures, standard for private companies. The semiconductor peer median of 20.5x P/S across public tickers remains unusable without target revenue.

Triangulation across applicable methods supports a range of $2.0B (low) to $6.0B (high), with a median of $3.8B. The current $3.75B valuation sits at the center of this range, reflecting both stage-driven progression and peer positioning. Key uncertainties include revenue scale relative to peers and differentiation within a crowded frontier-chip landscape; peer valuations themselves span an order of magnitude, limiting precision.
